system_description.narrative_title: Contested interdependence: summitry, markets, energy and tech frictions
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where great-power diplomacy and summitry (US-China-Russia) unfolds alongside active wars (Ukraine, broader Iran-related attacks), volatile energy flows and a resurgent oil surplus. Simultaneously, rising bond yields and hawkish central-bank expectations interact with geopolitical shocks, while export controls and an AI‑chip scandal are creating a new tech-containment layer that fractures supply chains and regional alignments. These dynamics produce reinforcing feedbacks — market stress, policy shifts, and diplomatic rifts — that propagate across regions and institutions even as climate and governance crises (COP31, climate finance) expose limits to collective responses.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, military conflicts and peace processes, global energy and commodity flows, international financial markets and central banks, technology and semiconductor supply chains (AI chips), multinational corporations and regulatory regimes, intergovernmental institutions and climate diplomacy; and the flows of capital, energy, information and military force that connect them.
system_description.super_system: The global international system — a political-economic-ecological world order integrating security, markets, technology, and planetary governance.
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security architectures (NATO/EU, Indo-Pacific, Middle East security complexes)
Global energy and commodity markets (oil, LNG, shipping routes)
International financial and monetary system (bond markets, central banks, cross-border capital)
Global technology and semiconductor supply chains (AI chips, export controls, industrial policy)

variables.name: US–China AI chip and export contest
variables.description: The United States, China and third-party hubs are contesting control of advanced AI chips and the export channels that supply them, as tighter US curbs, corporate scandals and rerouted supply chains reshape access and technological competition.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and fractured diplomacy
variables.description: Russia, Ukraine and their external backers remain locked in high-intensity warfare while fragmented negotiations, shifting European commitments and sanctions choices continuously reshape the conflict’s trajectory.

variables.name: Iran-centric regional escalation
variables.description: Iran, the United States and regional actors are involved in a widening pattern of strikes, proxy actions and nuclear-related tensions that are driving cross-border instability and complicating diplomatic efforts.

variables.name: Rebalancing of global oil flows and chokepoints
variables.description: Major producers and traders are driving a rapid market rebalancing from scarcity toward surplus as production rebounds, alternative export routes expand and episodic shipping disruptions reshape pricing and strategic leverage.

variables.name: Renewed monetary tightening and sovereign bond stress
variables.description: Major central banks and sovereign borrowers are confronting resurgent inflation pressures and hawkish rate expectations that are producing sharp bond-yield spikes, sovereign funding strains and cross-border capital shifts.
